title: Cloud Storage
objectives: Understand Cloud Storage via a real-life analogy
Secure files with Storage Rules (path, auth, contentType, size)
Serve images at scale (resize + CDN + client cache)

sections.markdown:
**Think of Cloud Storage for Firebase as a self-service parcel locker network.**

- Every **bucket** is a locker location (`gs://my-app.appspot.com`). Big storage capacity, globally replicated.
- Every **object** in the bucket is a labeled parcel — the label is its path (`users/u_abc/avatar.jpg`).
- **Uploading** is like dropping a parcel into a locker. The staff (rules) check your ID, verify the parcel isn't too heavy, and confirm it's an allowed item.
- **Downloading** is like retrieving a parcel — you show ID, staff hand it over.
- **Resumable uploads** — if the delivery van breaks down halfway, tomorrow it picks up where it left off (chunks + resume tokens).
- **Signed URLs** — a temporary 'pickup code' that anyone can use for 15 minutes to grab one specific parcel without ID.

**Under the hood, it's a wrapper around Google Cloud Storage (GCS)** — the same battle-tested object store powering YouTube. Firebase adds:
- Mobile-first SDK (progress events, retry logic, upload from `File` / `Uint8List`).
- Firebase-Auth-aware **Storage Rules** for path + auth + metadata checks.
- Integration with other Firebase services (Functions triggers on upload).

**Cost model:** you pay for STORAGE (bytes at rest), DOWNLOAD egress (bytes fetched by users), and OPERATIONS (uploads/downloads count). **Egress dominates** for image-heavy apps. Free tier: 5 GB stored, 1 GB/day downloaded, 20K uploads/day, 50K downloads/day.

**When to use:** user-uploaded avatars, photos, videos, PDFs, audio, ML model files, generated reports. **When NOT:** structured data (use Firestore/RTDB), tiny frequently-changing config (use RemoteConfig or Firestore), very hot public assets (put a CDN in front — cheaper egress).

**Every Flutter app with user-uploaded content uses this.** Interviews at Firebase-shop companies test path design, rules, and image-serving strategy. **Master this — it's a small topic but heavily tested.**

**Cloud Storage for Firebase** is Firebase's file storage service — a wrapper around Google Cloud Storage (GCS) with a mobile SDK. Handles user-uploaded files: images, videos, PDFs, audio. Features: resumable uploads/downloads, progress events, background transfer on iOS/Android, Firebase-Auth-aware Storage Rules. Data lives in **buckets** at paths like `users/{uid}/avatar.jpg`. Free tier: 5 GB stored, 1 GB/day download. Every Flutter app with user-generated content uses this.

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Client validates upload size.** Client is untrusted; rules must ALSO check `request.resource.size`.
**Mistake 2: Storing download URLs 'permanently' in Firestore.** URLs contain revocable download tokens; if you rotate a token, saved URLs break. Store the PATH; regenerate URL when needed.
**Mistake 3: Full-resolution downloads for thumbnails.** 5 MB image for a 100x100 avatar wastes 99% of bandwidth. Resize on upload.
**Mistake 4: No `contentType` validation.** Users upload `.exe` disguised as `.jpg`. Rules should enforce actual MIME type.
**Mistake 5: Not deleting Storage on user deletion.** GDPR requires it. Wire a Cloud Function on `auth.deleteUser` to recursively delete their subtree.
**Mistake 6: No upload progress UI.** Users abandon uploads at 30% because they think it's frozen. Show progress + cancel.
**Mistake 7: Uploading uncompressed camera images.** Compress client-side (image_picker's `imageQuality: 85`) before uploading — often 5x smaller with no visible loss.
## Best practices
**1. Path design.** `users/{uid}/{file}` — matches Auth UID → easy rules.
**2. Rules validate size + contentType** BEFORE upload lands.
**3. Resize on upload.** Firebase Extension → multi-size variants.
**4. CDN for hot public assets.** Cloud CDN cuts egress cost 4x.
**5. Client-side compression before upload.** `imageQuality: 85` on image_picker.
**6. Progress UI + cancel button.** Non-negotiable UX.
**7. Cache network images.** `cached_network_image` — free perf win.
**8. Cloud Function on user deletion** cleans their storage subtree (GDPR).
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy) — Avatar upload.** Upload a JPEG to `users/{uid}/avatar.jpg`; show progress; retrieve URL; display.
**Practice 2 (Medium) — Owner-only rules.** Rules restricting `users/{uid}/**` to matching UID; test with a second user; verify denial.
**Practice 3 (Medium) — Size + type validation.** Reject uploads > 5 MB and non-image; verify in rules unit tests.
**Practice 4 (Hard) — Resize extension + variants.** Install Resize Images extension; upload; verify multi-size variants; client picks size by need.
**Practice 5 (Hard) — Resumable upload.** Start upload; kill app; on relaunch resume from where it stopped.
**Practice 6 (Expert) — Signed URLs from a Function.** Cloud Function generates 15-min signed URL for a private file; client uses it once.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How do you secure uploads to Cloud Storage?**

**A:** **Storage Rules run server-side on every request** — client can't bypass. Rules can check: **(1) path** — `match /users/{uid}/{file}` with `request.auth.uid == uid`. **(2) auth** — `request.auth != null` and `request.auth.token.role`. **(3) size** — `request.resource.size < 5 * 1024 * 1024`. **(4) contentType** — `request.resource.contentType.matches('image/.*')`. **(5) cross-service checks** — `firestore.get(...).data` to check e.g., 'is this user a participant in the chat?'. **Critical:** rules evaluate BEFORE the file lands — huge uploads and wrong types are rejected at the edge, saving bandwidth. **Also enable App Check** — attests the request comes from your app. **Default deny** — always end with `match /{allPaths=**} { allow read, write: if false; }`. Client-side validation is a UX nicety; NEVER security. Every interview asks this.

**Q2: What's the difference between download URLs and signed URLs?**

**A:** **Download URLs** (Firebase-native) — `ref.getDownloadURL()`. Contains a **revocable token** in the URL. Never expires as long as the token is valid. Anyone with the URL can access the file — useful for public-ish assets. Revoke by generating a new token via the console → old URLs 404. Simple + free. **Signed URLs** (GCS-native) — generated server-side via a Cloud Function using the service-account key. Has an **explicit expiration** (`5 minutes`, `1 hour`, up to 7 days). More granular: can be scoped to specific HTTP verbs. Used when you want **temporary access** — email download links, one-off shares. Not directly available in the Firebase Flutter SDK — generate in a Function. **When to use each:** avatar/public content → download URL; private time-boxed shares → signed URL. **Don't store URLs long-term** — always regenerate; tokens can rotate.

**Q3: How do you serve images at scale?**

**A:** Four layers, each cutting cost + latency: **(1) Resize on upload** — Firebase Extension 'Resize Images' auto-generates size variants (100px, 400px, 1024px) when a new image lands. Client requests the size it needs — never full-res for a thumbnail. Typical savings: 90% bandwidth. **(2) CDN in front** — Firebase Storage egress ~$0.12/GB. Cloud CDN / Cloudflare ~$0.02-0.05/GB with edge caching. For popular assets, CDN is 4-6x cheaper. **(3) Client cache** — `cached_network_image` on Flutter caches to disk; repeat views are free. **(4) Progressive JPEGs + `memCacheWidth`** — decode at 2x display width, not full-res. **Real-world numbers:** an app that naively serves 5 MB avatars to 100K DAU costs ~$1000/mo in egress. With all four layers: ~$40/mo. **Every interview at Firebase-shop companies drills this**  — it's the difference between profitable and burning cash.

**Q4: How do resumable uploads work?**

**A:** Firebase Storage supports **chunked, resumable uploads** natively. The SDK: **(1)** Starts a session by POSTing to GCS with metadata → GCS returns a **session URI**. **(2)** Uploads the file in chunks (default 256 KB). **(3)** After each chunk, GCS ACKs how many bytes it received. **(4)** If the network drops or app crashes, the session URI is persisted to disk. On relaunch, the SDK queries GCS for the last-received byte + resumes from there. **Nothing is re-uploaded.** For a 100 MB video on a spotty 3G connection, this is essential — otherwise every drop restarts from 0. **API:** `task.pause()`, `task.resume()`, `task.cancel()`. Task state survives app restarts on iOS + Android. **Interview take:** 'The SDK does this for free. Devs just need to expose pause/cancel in the UI and show progress.'

**Q5: How do you audit Cloud Storage usage + costs?**

**A:** **(1) Firebase console → Storage → Usage** — bytes stored, egress, ops per day. Basic. **(2) Cloud Monitoring** — set alerts on `firebase_storage.googleapis.com/network/sent_bytes_count`. **(3) Access logs** — enable **Access Logs** on the underlying GCS bucket → every request logged to another bucket. Gnarly but complete. **(4) Cloud Functions on write** — log every upload to Firestore/BigQuery for granular analytics. **(5) Billing budget alerts** — set at $5, $50, $500 tiers; get notified before you're bleeding. **What to look for:** massive egress spikes (someone's app leaking?), tiny-file storms (should batch?), overlarge stored objects (unnecessary retention?), abandoned uploads (client failures). **Optimization loop:** find biggest cost driver → apply resize/CDN/cache/rules-limit → re-measure. **Every scaled Firebase app runs this loop monthly.** Senior interview topic.

**Q6: When would you NOT use Firebase Storage?**

**A:** **(1) Structured data** — use Firestore/RTDB (Storage is opaque bytes). **(2) High-frequency small object churn** — 20 ops/sec/object cap. **(3) Complex object metadata queries** — GCS metadata is a flat KV; if you need filters + joins, index metadata in Firestore. **(4) Global CDN at ultra-low latency** — Firebase Storage is regional; put Cloud CDN or Cloudflare in front. **(5) Extreme egress cost sensitivity** — heavy public assets: cheaper on Cloudflare R2 (zero egress) or S3+CloudFront. **(6) Peer-to-peer content sharing** — WebRTC / IPFS may fit better. **(7) Encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys** — GCS supports this but adds complexity; simpler solutions exist. **The senior skill:** know when it fits (user avatars, chat images, mobile-uploaded content, moderate-scale videos) vs when it doesn't (analytics blob storage, CDN-heavy static sites).

## Real-world usage

- **Every social app** — user avatars, photos, videos.
- **Chat apps** — image + video attachments.
- **E-commerce** — product photos.
- **User-generated content** platforms.
- **NOT for** — structured data (Firestore), heavy CDN workloads (dedicated CDN), P2P sharing.

## Advanced notes

- **Firebase Extensions** — Resize Images (one-click multi-size variants), Storage Reactions, etc.
- **Signed URLs** — Cloud Function with Admin SDK generates time-limited signed URLs.
- **Uniform bucket-level access** — turn off individual object ACLs; simpler + safer.
- **Object versioning** — GCS bucket setting; keeps prior versions on overwrite.
- **Lifecycle rules** — auto-delete objects after N days; move to Nearline/Coldline for cost.
- **Bucket location** — pick region close to users; multi-region for global apps.
- **Storage classes** — Standard (hot), Nearline (30d+), Coldline (90d+), Archive (365d+); tiered pricing.
- **CORS** — configure for web via `gsutil cors`.
- **Cross-project bucket** — Firebase project can access buckets in other GCP projects.
- **Object hold / retention** — legal hold to prevent deletion (compliance).
- **Object metadata** — custom key-value; use for tagging.
- **Change data feed** — Cloud Function triggers on `finalize` (upload) / `delete`.
- **Encryption** — encrypted-at-rest by default; optional customer-managed keys via KMS.
- **VPC-SC** — perimeter for high-security enterprise buckets.
- **Upload rate limits** — 5 QPS/writes to a single object; 20 QPS/writes across a bucket after warmup.
